MIDI-GUIDED MUSIC SYNTHESIS AND EDITING

SpanSynth-Edit

Synthesis and editing of multi-instrument audio mixtures.

Repo↗ Dataset referenceComing soon DataComing soon Listen to the demos ↓

Abstract

We introduce SpanSynth-Edit, a flow-matching model for MIDI-guided synthesis and editing of multi-instrument audio mixtures in low-frame-rate scalar-quantized latents. Its MIDI Span representation encodes the lifecycle of each instrument-labeled note as events aligned with audio-latent frames. Within each frame, MIDI events form an unordered set with continuous-valued numerical attributes. Contextual audio provides instrument-specific timbre guidance. Our model also supports region-specific editing by resynthesizing the target region from revised MIDI. Experiments show competitive synthesis and editing performance across single- and multi-instrument benchmarks and demonstrate acoustic sensitivity to slight MIDI onset shifts. We also discuss the limitations of transcription-based note-adherence evaluation.

Listening conditions

Early demos reuse the original audio files from the earlier model, with their original listening levels. Model comparison uses the current Base SQ model. Those comparisons use one gain per SpanSynth output, estimated from its surrounding audio, while other systems’ generated sections are matched to the reference level. All players within a comparison share any final attenuation needed for headroom.

No limiter, crossfade, or time stretching is applied. MIDI shows the input instructions, not a transcription of generated audio.
